_comment: Authored input for scripts/render-glossary.js. Only the prose lives here.
Skill names, categories, postures, legacy flags, versions and file paths are read
from buildMarketplace() and the catalogue markers at render time, so they cannot
be retyped wrong. Keys are the published skill name; rename_pairs lets one entry
serve either side of an accepted rename.
Keep every 'what' and 'why' to one line. When a row needs a paragraph, the content
belongs in the catalogue entry, not here.

agent-platform-context.what: EnGenAI agent-runtime internals: executor, mailbox messaging, lead/worker teams, Celery lifecycle.
agent-platform-context.why: Background reading for legacy platform code; it is not current Kaidera truth.

api-design.what: Legacy FastAPI conventions for URLs, request/response schemas, auth, pagination, errors and OpenAPI.
api-design.why: Pattern reference in a repository that already matches; verify against current source first.

api-test.what: Legacy FastAPI contract and integration test structure, AsyncClient use, auth fixtures, async DB mocks.
api-test.why: Test-shape ideas only; it runs nothing and never supports a coverage claim.

assert-fact-gate.what: Blocks any factual claim until a fresh source check in this turn backs it.
assert-fact-gate.why: Cheapest honesty control in the portfolio: kills recalled SHAs, “tests pass” and “it’s deployed”.

assumption-validation.what: Separates “the code is correct” from “this costly, customer-visible assumption is supported”.
assumption-validation.why: Run before ranking, pricing, quota, default or migration changes that tests cannot judge.

backend-context.what: Legacy FastAPI service-layer, async DB access, authentication, middleware and security conventions.
backend-context.why: Orientation inside old backend code; resolve every fact against the owning repository.

code-review.what: Legacy two-stage checklist: specification compliance, then code quality, ending in a verdict.
code-review.why: Historical reference only; its merge and log postconditions exceed its no-tool contract.

security-review-checklist.what: Legacy product security checklist covering auth, secrets, tenant isolation and supply chain.
security-review-checklist.why: A supporting lens under an evidence-gated review; never a competing verdict.

container-build.what: Legacy multi-stage image builds, non-root UID, hardening, CI build pipeline and registry push.
container-build.why: Hardening ideas; note it disagrees with `k8s-deploy` on region and service names.

database-migration.what: Legacy Alembic and PostgreSQL migration naming, safe practice, rollback, data migration and RLS patterns.
database-migration.why: Pattern reference; its migration head disagrees with `backend-context`.

dependency-audit.what: Legacy CVE scanning, supply-chain verification, dependency pinning and remediation workflow.
dependency-audit.why: Installs and runs scanners while declaring no tools; split into separate workflows before reuse.

deploy-gate.what: Gates push, pull request, merge, release and deploy on exact target, current authority, evidence and rollback.
deploy-gate.why: The last deterministic stop before anything irreversible leaves the machine.

deploy-to-dev.what: Legacy GitOps runbook: sprint-branch push triggers CI, image build, gitops update and ArgoCD sync.
deploy-to-dev.why: Names one retired product's environment; its hostnames and project identifiers are now placeholders. Do not generalise it.

development-workflow.what: Portable AI-plus-human lifecycle: bounded tasks, independent review, risk-based QA, recorded decisions.
development-workflow.why: The generic SDLC profile for development projects; select exactly one lifecycle owner per project.

frontend-context.what: Legacy Next.js 14 App Router, React Flow, Tailwind, Zustand and strict-TypeScript conventions.
frontend-context.why: Orientation inside old frontend code only.

gavel.what: Typed, probabilistic judgments on a lead’s three decision moments: a return, a handoff, a backlog order.
gavel.why: A calibrated second opinion before you rule. Mutually exclusive with the Jev lead wrappers.

git-workflow.what: Legacy conventional commits, branch strategy, sprint branching, pull-request process and merge rules.
git-workflow.why: Describes Git mutation under a no-tool manifest; rework before use.

human-voice.what: Drafts, rewrites or audits public prose so it carries checkable specifics and a named person’s voice.
human-voice.why: Removes machine-generic copy from posts, articles, email, decks, newsletters and web pages.

incident-response.what: Legacy incident runbook: classification, blast-radius containment, kill switch, evidence, post-incident review.
incident-response.why: Its containment-before-preservation ordering is unsafe; rebuild human-gated before any use.

infra-naming-gate.what: Validates infrastructure names against an organisation, project, environment, role, locality and ordinal grammar.
infra-naming-gate.why: Prevents resources that cannot later be renamed and collisions across projects.

infrastructure-context.what: Legacy GKE, ArgoCD GitOps, Terraform, Helm, CI/CD pipeline and hardening overview.
infrastructure-context.why: Orientation inside old infrastructure code only.

jev.what: Reference for the shared Jev core, project transfer policy, CLI, result statuses and the four wrappers.
jev.why: Setup and troubleshooting. It is not an automatic decision-moment router; install wrappers separately.

jev-backlog-rank.what: Checks an accountable lead’s backlog ordering against stated gate dependencies and delay risk.
jev-backlog-rank.why: Catches mis-sequenced dispatch waves early; the human keeps priority authority.

jev-handoff-check.what: Inspects a drafted worker handoff’s receipt contract, gate, exclusions and blocked protocol before sending.
jev-handoff-check.why: Stops dispatches that no worker could ever prove completion against.

jev-option-decision.what: Examines one bounded implementation or architecture choice with named candidates, evidence and requirements.
jev-option-decision.why: Structured option comparison for a decision that is genuinely open; the accountable person decides.

jev-return-triage.what: Advisory receipt-based triage of an arrived worker return, handback or consult.
jev-return-triage.why: Separates acceptable work from rework before the lead rules on it.

k8s-deploy.what: Legacy Kubernetes manifests, resource limits, health probes, ArgoCD workflow, Helm charts and GKE config.
k8s-deploy.why: Pattern reference; contradicts `container-build` on region and services.

kaidera-sdlc.what: The Kaidera loop: intent, grill, spec, plan, build, verify, review, ship, maintain, re-enter from incidents.
kaidera-sdlc.why: The operating method every lead runs. Nothing is implemented without an accepted plan.

marketing-web-research.what: Researches companies, current decision makers and professional profiles from public and authorised sessions.
marketing-web-research.why: Market mapping, leadership lists and follow reconciliation. Research never authorises contact.

open-code-review.what: Diff-first, evidence-gated review of a bounded change: exact receipt, diagnostics, impact, challenge, coverage.
open-code-review.why: The portfolio’s change-review contract. Strictly read-only. Collides by name with Alibaba’s distinct skill.

performance-profiling.what: Legacy Python async, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes and Redis profiling for latency-regression diagnosis.
performance-profiling.why: Runs live production diagnostics while declaring no tools; rework before use.

prompt-injection-test-design.what: Read-only design checklist for testing a skill-content injection boundary: threats, corpus, rejection criteria.
prompt-injection-test-design.why: Designs a separately controlled harness; it embeds no payloads and executes nothing.

prompt-master.what: Vendored verbatim from the donor: writes one optimised prompt for a named AI tool from a rough request.
prompt-master.why: Only on an explicit prompt-engineering request. Donor name, licence and attribution are preserved.

research-brief.what: Turns an ambiguous research request into a self-contained, decision-led brief with a source plan.
research-brief.why: Drafts the mission. It performs no research, invokes no vendor, spends nothing, contacts nobody.

route-handoff-gate.what: Verifies project, lane, layer, role and dependency boundaries before work is created or rerouted.
route-handoff-gate.why: Prevents cross-lane and wrong-project dispatch, the most common multi-agent failure.

scope-work-gate.what: Confirms proposed work belongs to the current project, role, lane and approved objective.
scope-work-gate.why: Stops “while we’re here” scope creep before it starts, not after review.

security-context.what: Legacy threat model, OWASP Top 10 checklist, forbidden patterns and required security controls.
security-context.why: Reference lens; its control claims are unverified against current source.

sprint-closing.what: Legacy six-phase sprint closure: documentation, commit, push and pull-request procedure.
sprint-closing.why: Names one individual as approver and one product as scope; not portable.

sprint-context.what: Legacy three-file sprint pattern, TASK_STATUS protocol, definition of done and quality gates.
sprint-context.why: Workflow assumptions no longer match Kaidera delivery; rework before use.

tdd-workflow.what: Legacy red-green-refactor loop with a five-step verification requirement before “done”.
tdd-workflow.why: Describes test execution under a no-tool manifest; the discipline is sound, the contract is not.

ultrareview.what: Whole-codebase or module health audit across eight dimensions with adversarial verification of findings.
ultrareview.why: Repository-wide scope. Its opt-in fix mode exceeds its declared no-tool contract.

unlazy.what: Completion discipline: write acceptance gates first, decompose with a depth tree, re-measure every claim.
unlazy.why: The counter to quiet incompleteness on long, multi-part, parallel or exhaustive work.

workspace-context.what: Legacy workspace identity, tech stack, team structure, terminology and development principles.
workspace-context.why: Orientation only; it names a retired organisation and product.

cloud-agnostic-policy.what: Reviews infrastructure choices for portability and blocks undeclared provider-specific managed primitives.
cloud-agnostic-policy.why: Apply before architecture locks in; enforces portable, upstream-OSS-only infrastructure.

investor-lead-gen.what: Finds investors for an early-stage round, writes to each person one to one, follows up once and hands replies to the owners.
investor-lead-gen.why: Investor lead generation with a portable investor database and a weekly learning loop. Research never authorises a send.

renames.why: Says “checklist” so no router mistakes it for a verdict engine, and drops the `code-review` stem that collides with the review family.
The skill designs a test harness and executes nothing; the bare name reads as a runnable test.
Removes a live identity collision: Alibaba ships a different skill under this exact name, and agent trees have installed both. States the evidence contract the skill actually enforces.
A branded superlative says nothing about scope. The new name states whole-repository scope and separates it from bounded-change review.
A personality label. The new name states the outcome the skill produces.

**Withdrawn after execution.** Two facts the owner did not have when approving it: the mandate this gate enforces is itself named “Cloud-Agnostic, Fully-Portable, Upstream-OSS-Only”, so the new name drops the word the mandate leads with; and four prose cross-references in the consuming agent tree cite the old name. The rename would manufacture a third identity for one control rather than resolve the two that already exist. The sibling-`-gate` consistency argument is real, and weaker than both.

**Withdrawn.** This manifest is a projection: it carries `kaidera.source` and is regenerated from a canonical directory in another repository, so a rename applied here is overwritten at the next render and desynchronises the skill from the family it belongs to. A projected skill inherits its name from its source owner.
Retirement declined by the owner on 2026-10-07. The name stays; the skill is now filed under `legacy/`, which is what stops a router from preferring it over the evidence-gated reviewer.
Retirement declined by the owner on 2026-10-07. The name stays; the skill is now filed under `legacy/`.

renames.proposed: keep the name, move to the design category
renames.why: The product prefix is correct because the rulebook is product-specific, but `development` is the wrong category once `design/` exists.
“Gated” describes the form, not the artifact. A landing page is what it builds.
“Navigator” does not say what it produces, and the name sits next to `social-channel-research`, which covers the same platform read-only. The split that matters is research versus account action.
“Fitness” is a metaphor; the job is choosing which model each worker runs.

in_flight.name: adaptech-uiux-design
in_flight.what: Governing UI/UX and design-system rulebook for the ASW Connect / AdapTech dark-aviation products.
in_flight.why: Enforces one house style, computed WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and an elevation ladder for that product only.

in_flight.name: folder-organisation
in_flight.what: One root, one home per kind of thing, one owner per fact — plus the loop that consolidates a scattered estate.
in_flight.why: Placement gate before creating any document, diagram, plan, proof, pack or worktree, and before deleting a folder.

in_flight.name: linkedin-navigator
in_flight.what: Builds LinkedIn follow and connect target lists with no API, no login session and no paid scraper.
in_flight.why: Turns a named account list into a click-through checklist; a human performs every account action.

in_flight.name: model-fitness
in_flight.what: Reviews which model each project worker runs, gathers public and tester feedback, recommends best per task.
in_flight.why: Use for roster audits, an underperforming worker, a new model release, or a fitness question.

in_flight.name: social-channel-research
in_flight.what: Source-linked, read-only research on public LinkedIn, X and Instagram content through authorised host channels.
in_flight.why: Stops when a platform needs an unavailable login or permission; never publishes or interacts with accounts.

in_flight.name: kaidera-deck-design
in_flight.what: Designs, builds and checks house-style investor and partner decks as a scripted PPTX with PDF export.
in_flight.why: Repeatable deck quality with a recorded QA pass. Writes local files only; never sends or publishes.

in_flight.name: gated-deck-web-page
in_flight.what: Turns an approved deck into an unlisted static page that emails the PDF after a name, title and address.
in_flight.why: Lead capture on a deck. It does not deploy the page, build the endpoint or send the email.

in_flight.name: lead-generation-outreach
in_flight.what: Finds, qualifies and verifies prospective customers, then contacts each one personally by email.
in_flight.why: Drafts from cited evidence, queues each batch for owner approval, records every send, stops on any reply.

consumed_third_party.name: ci-security-scanning-with-strix
consumed_third_party.what: Diff-scoped AI pentest as a CI/CD pre-merge gate, with SARIF to code scanning.

consumed_third_party.name: fix-security-vulnerabilities-with-strix
consumed_third_party.what: Root-cause remediation of validated Strix findings, re-scanned to prove closure.

consumed_third_party.name: managed-pentesting-with-strix
consumed_third_party.what: Pentest-as-a-service through the hosted API: schedules, webhooks, auditor-ready reports.

consumed_third_party.name: penetration-testing-with-strix
consumed_third_party.what: Autonomous pentest that exploits and proves vulnerabilities instead of flagging them.

consumed_third_party.name: typesafe-ai
consumed_third_party.what: Typed AI primitives (System One models) for routing, ranking, extraction and verification in product code.

consumed_third_party.name: pr
consumed_third_party.what: Pull-request body writing. Pinned in the consuming project’s skills lockfile.

consumed_third_party.name: retro
consumed_third_party.what: Coding-session retrospective, on explicit request only. Pinned in the lockfile.

consumed_third_party.name: writing-for-agents
consumed_third_party.what: Writing documents that agents consume: skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md. Pinned in the lockfile.
